## Summary

The 68080 integer unit is a 3-operand unit with access to D0–D7 and E0–E23 through the BANK prefix, B0–B7 address registers, superscalar execution and instruction fusing.

## Details

- The 68080 integer unit is a 3 operand unit. It has access to 4 times as many data registers, D0..7 & E0..23. This is done by the BANK prefix. Many instructions can use e-registers. The 3 operand is not supported by that yet.
- Multiple instructions can be done at the same time.
- 1: Superscalar like the 060 in another unit.
- 2: Fuse two instructions by using 64bit or 3 operand.

```asm
    move.l (a0)+,(a1)+  &  move.l (a0)+,(a1)+		Fuse to 64bit.
    move.l #120,d2  &  add.l d1,d2  → add.l #120,d1,d2	Fuse to 3 operand.
```

- Conditional instruction: Single instruction after bcc.s.

```asm
   bcc.s skip
   <one_single_cycle_instruction>
skip
```

- The 080 has 2 times as much address registers. A0..7 & B0..7.
- The b-registers are fully interchangeable for ammx instructions, but not for the legacy instructions.
- The addressing unit can handle almost all &lt;ea&gt; that where not possible on instructions with previous cpu's. Pc-relative is a good example of that. However pc-relative as destination is currently not calculated correct when some rarly used extended format is used for the source operand. (v2 users do not use pc-dest.)
- Registers are 64bit, but integer uses 32bit so movem.l is enough to multitask older programs. Except bitfield, that oddly extends to 64 bit for now.

### Integer instructions that use e-registers

- move(q),addi, subi eor(i),ori, andi, not, neg(x), (b)tst, (b)clr, bset, swap, scc
- bf(clr/set/tst/chg), ext(u), cmpi, as(r/l), ls(r/l), ro(x)(r/l), moviw.l, perm
- handling of banking not correct yet:
- pack, unpk, mul, div, abcd, sbcd, movex, add, sub,and, or, cmp, addx, subx
- exg, bf(extu/exts/ffo/ins)

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- 68000–68060 integer instructions are 2-operand. The 68080 adds a third operand (through BANK), E and B registers, fusing, and conditional execution of a single instruction after BCC.S.

## Do / Don't

- DON'T rely on banking for: pack, unpk, mul, div, abcd, sbcd, movex, add, sub, and, or, cmp, addx, subx, exg, bfextu, bfexts, bfffo, bfins. The manual says banking is not handled correctly yet for these.
